rationale: This is a rank-preserving monotone transform of the archived NearTermCashRequirementCoverage, so the sort-based portfolio evidence is essentially mechanically unchanged and only the FMB slope can move — a cosmetic functional-form tweak rather than a new mechanism, with the added defect that LOG is undefined whenever the numerator (capx+aqc+dlc+dvc) is non-positive, silently trimming coverage.

Smoothing only the requirement leg is a genuine (not merely monotone) change that tests persistence against a fixed functional form, and the timing asymmetry is defensible, though it remains a close relative of an archived ratio and inherits the same LOG-domain fragility.

The expression matches the hypothesis with clean, non-overlapping roles for plant, cash and requirements, and the sign logic is internally consistent, but it is the archive's standard MUL(rank-conditioner, rank-difference) template with the need leg swapped, so it is an incremental permutation rather than a new economic idea.

The first difference of the dependence state is a distinct and untested economic event that is roughly orthogonal to the level, though it overlaps materially with the published abnormal-capital-investment/investment-growth anomaly and will be dominated by lumpy year-to-year swings in capx and current debt.

An equal-weight rank sum of high investment, low cash and share issuance is a direct restatement of three separately published anomalies (asset/investment growth, cash holdings, net share issuance) bundled together, and by the proposer's own framing it is an operator-structure retest of an already-evaluated population rather than a new mechanism.

The multi-year liquidity trajectory is a genuinely new conditioner and the sign direction is coherent, but the product of two non-negative ranks makes the low end ambiguous (either leg near zero suffices), so the claimed "fortress balance sheet" long leg is not what the expression actually isolates.
